newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk minister orders compliance with dress laws.
newsitem.headline: Turk minister orders compliance with dress laws.

text.p: Turkey's Health Minister Yildirim Aktuna has ordered provincial governors to ensure public health workers comply with laws that ban wearing religious dress, a ministry official said on Monday.
"I think the order was made in the framework of the National Security Council decisions," the official told Reuters.
Turkey's military dominated security council last month ordered the country's first Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan to crack down on rising Islamist activism.
Among their demands was the enforcement of the Islamic dress ban, as well as action to close down Islamist sects and rein in illegal religious instruction classes.

The dress codes, set by the founder of secularist Turkey Mustafa Kemal Ataturk in 1920s, officially oblige public workers to dress in western-style clothing -- skirts for women and ties for men -- during working hours.

But the the enforcement of the codes has lapsed in recent years with some female public workers wearing Islamic headscarves to work and others asking for permission to dress in full Islamic garb, Turkish media said.
Aktuna said earlier that he was not hopeful that Erbakan's ruling Welfare Party would support measures to crack down on Islamist activism.
Aktuna's comments helped push shares down in Istanbul by 4.49 percent at the end of the day over concerns about the future of the coalition and rumours that he was about to resign.
